sources.note: layout sqft clusters derived from URA transactions

development.orientation_notes: Marketed as N–S oriented (units predominantly face north/south, which limits harsh direct E–W sun — favourable for SG). Two pools (Olympic-length grand pool + reflective pool): the practical consequence is that genuinely QUIET-facing units are scarce — most stacks face either a road or a pool (pool-side carries children's-pool noise). Some ground-floor units have private enclosed pools (PES). Balcony size grows with floor — high-floor balconies are ~2× the low-floor ones. Per-stack numbered facing NOT verified from text — needs the visual site plan.
known_issues: Quiet-facing units are scarce — most stacks face a road or one of the two pools (kids'-pool noise) [StackedHomes tour]
Stacks fronting Compassvale Rd / the elevated rail corridor: road + train noise — though a resident notes some road sides are light-traffic and HDB-buffered [StackedHomes]
Low-floor units get noticeably smaller balconies than high-floor units [StackedHomes]
99-yr leasehold from 2011 — lease-decay clock already running

layouts.notes: Smallest layout; thin resale cohort (few transact).
Most liquid 2BR band (775 sqft is the volume layout).
1001 sqft has the better living/dining; large for a 2BR so psf-rent yield dilutes.
Large top-floor units; trade at low psf for size — not a value signal.
